sentences.text:
Order 
Per: Justice Vishal Dhagat Appellant has filed appeal under Section 19(1) of Family Courts Act, 1984 challenging judgment and decree dated 25.04.2025 passed in RCSHM No. 201/2022 by Second Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Jabalpur (M.P.).

entities.text: Second Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: By judgment and decree, suit preferred by appellant for divorce was dismissed by trial Court.

2. Counsel appearing for appellant submitted that marriage between appellant and respondent took place according to Hindu rites and rituals on 28.01.1992 at Ijgaon, District Adilabad (Andhra Pradesh).
Out of wedlock, appellant and respondent were blessed with two daughters namely Deepika Mandal and Supriya Mandal, who are major.
Dispute between the parties started after some time and they started living separately since year 2002.

It NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:68948 2 FA-751-2025 is stated that respondent performed second marriage on 04.07.2002 with one Malti Pal D/o Gopal Pal, R/o Ijgaon, District Adilabad (A.P.).
A complaint was filed at Jabalpur bearing Criminal Complaint Case No. 121/2004 on 12.08.2002 for offences punishable under Sections 294, 120-B, 506-B, 420, 496, 406 and 494 of Indian Penal Code.
During pendency of complaint case, appellant had performed second marriage on 13.04.2011 and she is practicing as an Advocate at District Court, Jabalpur since year 2020.

Respondent had also filed a suit for declaring second marriage between appellant and one Hitendra Chudasama dated Smt. Shikharani Mandal vs Dhananjay Mandal on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/1845091/
1 13.04.2011 to be null and void.
Suit was allowed by Family Court, Jabalpur vide judgment and decree dated 29.10.2018 and marriage was declared as null and void.
Lately, second husband Hitendra Chudasama of appellant died on 28.03.2024.
Counsel appearing for appellant submitted that appellant and respondent are living separately for last more than 20 years.
Trial Court had committed an error in not allowing suit filed by appellant.
Document Ex.P/1 was not taken into consideration.
Appellant had preferred appeal against judgment and decree passed by Family Court declaring her marriage dated 13.04.2011 to be null and void, but same was withdrawn due to death of second husband.

3. Counsel appearing for appellant has relied upon judgment passed by Apex Court in case of Samar Ghosh vs Jaya Ghosh, reported in (2007) 4 SCC 511, wherein it was held that in cases of long period of continuous separation, it may fairly be concluded that matrimonial bond is beyond repair.

entities.text: Samar Ghosh vs Jaya Ghosh, reported in (2007) 4 SCC 511
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Marriage only becomes a fiction.
In such cases, non severing of ties may lead to mental cruelty.
C o u n s e l f o r a p p e l l a n t s u b m i t t e d t h a t r e s p o n d e n t N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .
2025:MPHC-JBP:68948 3 FA-751-2025 had remarried.
They are living separately for long i.e. from 2002.
There is irretrievable breakdown of marriage between the parties.
Appellant tried to patch up the marriage and there was compromise agreement also, but thereafter again she was beaten up and she left the house.
In these circumstances, Court ought to have allowed the appeal preferred by appellant.
4. Respondent refused to take notice.
On 15.07.2025, Registry has directed office to proceed in accordance with Rule 11(1) and (2) of High Court of Madhya Pradesh Rules, 2008.

entities.text: High Court of Madhya Pradesh Rules, 2008
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: According to said Rule, if party refuses to accept notice, then party is treated to be served.
In view of same, respondent is proceeded exparte.

5. Heard the counsel for appellant.
6.
Appellant had pleaded that respondent demanded Rs. 3 lacs in dowry and blamed appellant to bring less dowry.
She was mentally and physically harassed.
Respondent used to work as Dry Cleaner and used to spent money earned from said business on drinking liquor and on other women.
He also used to beat her.

When matter was reported to family members by appellant,
compromise took place between them on 18.04.2002 and she started living with him.
She was again beaten up on 24.04.2002 and thereafter, she left the house of her husband.
It is submitted that on 04.07.2002, respondent got married with another woman namely Malti Pal.
She filed complaint case and made respondent and said woman as party in the case, which is still pending.

It is submitted that in said circumstances, appellant has also re-married to one Hitendra Chudasama,
but said marriage was declared to be null and void NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:68948 4 FA-751-2025 as she was having one living spouse.
She challenged said judgment and decree, but meanwhile husband died and therefore, appeal was withdrawn.
Prayer was made to grant decree of divorce on ground of cruelty and desertion.
She had deposed before Court regarding aforesaid fact.
She had stated in Court that she was continuously beaten up and treated with cruelty by respondent.
Respondent had done second married.
Appellant had sent notice to respondent when he did second marriage.
Complaint case was registered and order-sheets of said case were filed in Court as Ex.P/1.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Trial Court considered pleadings and evidence available on record and held that no police complaint was lodged by appellant.
No documentary evidence was produced before Court regarding second marriage.
There was minor disputes between husband and wife, which will not amount to cruelty.
Trial Court further took into account the fact that appellant had suppressed factum of compromise between them.
If appellant had started living again with respondent, therefore, she had forgiven the cruelty of respondent to her and she cannot rely upon aforesaid fact.
Appellant failed to prove her case and she cannot take benefit of weaknesses of respondent's case.
Appellant did not file any application for restitution of conjugal rights nor called any panchayat or meetings of society for restitution of matrimonial status.
Appellant did not file any police complaint regarding harassment.
In these circumstances, Trial Court found that case was not proved and suit was dismissed.

8. Considering totality of facts and circumstances of the case, it is found that appellant and respondent are living separately since 2002 i.e. for more NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:68948 5 FA-751-2025 than 23 years as on today.

During intervening period,
appellant got remarried and her marriage was declared null and void.
Later on, her second husband also died.
There was allegation that respondent had also married, but trial Court failed to take into consideration complaint case filed by appellant.
Said complaint case is said to be pending in trial Court.

9. Considering aforesaid circumstances, it is found that there is irretrievable breakdown of marriage between appellant and respondent and there is no possibility of resumption of marital ties between them.
Both of them are settled in their own lives.

10. Considering aforesaid circumstances, appeal filed by appellant is allowed and judgement and decree dated 25.04.2025 passed in RCSHM No. 201/2022 by Second Additional Principal Judge,
Family Court, Jabalpur is set aside.

11. Decree of divorce be prepared accordingly.
12. Appeal is allowed and disposed off.
